subject: Creative Arts
source: NaCCA Creative Arts Curriculum for Primary Schools, Basic 4–6 (September 2019)
accessibility: Read prompts and choices aloud when needed. Practical responses may use classroom materials, movement, speech or drawing.

indicators.statement: Study and talk about visual artworks created by selected Ghanaian visual artists that reflect the history and culture of the people of Ghana.
indicators.content_standard: B4.1.1.1 Generate ideas for artistic expression from people, culture, environment and topical issues.

skills.description: Identify the subject, artistic method and evidence in a work.
Study and describe in visual arts.
Use artistic evidence to explain a choice or improvement.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. What is this work about?
options: Reducing waste with reusable things
Canoes on a Ghanaian shore
Waste blocking a drain
A group represented by its flag
questions.answer: A group represented by its flag
hints: Identify the action or subject at the centre.
questions.explanation: The described action centres on a group represented by its flag.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which detail could a learner point out in the work?
options: Joined hands at the centre of the flag
A bottle shape printed on a cloth bag
Arrows stopping at a pile of waste
A row of dark boats along a pale curve
questions.answer: Joined hands at the centre of the flag
hints: Look for a detail the example actually describes.
questions.explanation: The evidence in the example is joined hands at the centre of the flag.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which method is used?
options: Placing contrasting scenes side by side
Repeating a cut-paper printing shape
Stitching and arranging fabric samples
Arranging a clear symbol on coloured bands
questions.answer: Arranging a clear symbol on coloured bands
hints: Think about how the parts were made or performed.
questions.explanation: The example uses arranging a clear symbol on coloured bands to show a group represented by its flag.

questions.stem: A pot has a wide mouth and two handles. What might its handles help a person do?
options: Lift the pot
Make it deeper
Close its mouth
Change its colour
questions.answer: Lift the pot
hints: Look at the way hands could hold it.
questions.explanation: Look at the way hands could hold it. Lift the pot.

questions.stem: Which words describe a pattern you can see on cloth?
options: Triangles repeat along the edge.
The cloth must be very old.
The maker was in a hurry.
Everyone likes the cloth.
questions.answer: Triangles repeat along the edge.
hints: Describe what the eye can check.
questions.explanation: Describe what the eye can check. Triangles repeat along the edge.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which idea does the work suggest?
options: People use the shore as a landing place
Repair can extend the life of cloth
The class values working together
Keeping drains clear lets water pass
questions.answer: The class values working together
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: The detail of joined hands at the centre of the flag supports the idea that the class values working together.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which source would help the class check its account?
options: The exchange class's pictures of things used again
A labelled photograph of the artist's coastal subject
A labelled account of Theodosia Okoh's flag design
Observations of water flowing in a school drain
questions.answer: A labelled account of Theodosia Okoh's flag design
hints: Choose evidence about the actual subject.
questions.explanation: The closest source for this subject is a labelled account of Theodosia Okoh's flag design.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which sentence describes evidence before giving an opinion?
options: Everybody will like the finished piece.
The work will win first prize.
The maker must have found the work easy.
Joined hands at the centre of the flag.
questions.answer: Joined hands at the centre of the flag.
hints: Choose a detail you can check in the example.
questions.explanation: Joined hands at the centre of the flag. This detail can be checked without guessing what someone thinks.

questions.stem: A rough rock and a smooth bottle appear in a drawing. What is the artist showing by changing the marks on their surfaces?
options: The price
The date
Texture
The title
questions.answer: Texture
hints: Imagine how each surface would feel.
questions.explanation: Imagine how each surface would feel. Texture.

questions.stem: A drawing shows tiny figures beside a large tree. Which part suggests the tree's size?
options: The frame is brown.
The figures are small beside it.
The paper has four corners.
The drawing has a title.
questions.answer: The figures are small beside it.
hints: Compare the sizes within the picture.
questions.explanation: Compare the sizes within the picture. The figures are small beside it.

questions.stem: Which question asks an artist about the meaning of a work?
options: When does the building close?
What did you want people to understand?
How many chairs are in the room?
How long is the wall beside the work?
questions.answer: What did you want people to understand?
hints: Meaning is about the idea the artist communicates.
questions.explanation: Meaning is about the idea the artist communicates. What did you want people to understand?.

questions.stem: You want to learn what has changed over time. Which pair would help most?
options: Two copies of the same photograph
Two guesses about the maker's name
Two labels for the same display shelf
An older example and a recent one from the same community
questions.answer: An older example and a recent one from the same community
hints: Look for evidence from two times.
questions.explanation: Look for evidence from two times. An older example and a recent one from the same community.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which change would make the main detail easier to recognise?
options: Turn some boat shapes towards the landing
Give the hands a colour that stands out from the bands
Leave a clear path between the stalls and the water
Make the stopped arrows visible beside the waste
questions.answer: Give the hands a colour that stands out from the bands
hints: Keep the aim and strengthen the clue the audience needs.
questions.explanation: This change helps the audience notice joined hands at the centre of the flag.

questions.stem: Pupils study Theodosia Okoh's flag design before making a class flag. How can they learn from it while making a new design?
options: Trace Ghana's flag and claim to have invented it.
Keep only the flagpole and leave the subject undecided.
Choose a meaningful symbol for their own group and make it easy to see.
Copy the date from a label as the whole design.
questions.answer: Choose a meaningful symbol for their own group and make it easy to see.
hints: Notice how a symbol can express identity.
questions.explanation: Notice how a symbol can express identity. Choose a meaningful symbol for their own group and make it easy to see.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. A partner wants to know why the artist chose this method. Which reply explains the choice?
options: It shows the artist used the most costly tools.
It proves this is the only way to make the piece.
It guarantees that everyone will have the same feeling.
It helps show a group represented by its flag.
questions.answer: It helps show a group represented by its flag.
hints: Ask what this choice helps the audience notice.
questions.explanation: Arranging a clear symbol on coloured bands helps communicate the subject through joined hands at the centre of the flag.

questions.stem: What can you learn by looking closely at the edge of a woven basket?
options: The song its maker sang
How the strips cross and turn
The name of its next owner
The date it will be sold
questions.answer: How the strips cross and turn
hints: Look for visible clues to the making.
questions.explanation: Look for visible clues to the making. How the strips cross and turn.

questions.stem: Which note will help you find the work you studied again?
options: Its title, maker and where you found it
Your seat number and the time you stood up
The colour of the notebook you used
The number of people who left first
questions.answer: Its title, maker and where you found it
hints: Write down details that identify the source.
questions.explanation: Write down details that identify the source. Its title, maker and where you found it.

questions.stem: A picture shows a market long ago. Which detail could help you learn about work there?
options: The number of corners on its label
The tools in the sellers' hands
The colour of the museum door
The day you visited the picture
questions.answer: The tools in the sellers' hands
hints: Find evidence inside the picture.
questions.explanation: Find evidence inside the picture. The tools in the sellers' hands.

questions.stem: A visitor says a work feels joyful. What would turn this feeling into an explanation?
options: Repeat the word joyful more loudly
Write the price next to the title
Point to a feature that gives that impression
Count the visitors who came in that day
questions.answer: Point to a feature that gives that impression
hints: Connect a feeling to something in the work.
questions.explanation: Connect a feeling to something in the work. Point to a feature that gives that impression.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. What do you notice about a group represented by its flag? Describe one detail in the example and explain what it tells you about life in Ghana.
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: For example, connect joined hands at the centre of the flag to the idea that the class values working together. Other supported choices are welcome.

Describes a detail and links it to the subject or setting.

Placing contrasting scenes side by side

questions.stem: A learner has drawn an idea for a round container. What else should the learner draw to help plan it?
options: The name of an unrelated song
A second signature
A price without a drawing
A side view showing its depth
questions.answer: A side view showing its depth
hints: A flat view may hide the container's form.

questions.stem: You like the woven lines on a basket. Which idea uses that observation in a new design?
options: Trace the whole basket label
Draw crossing bands on a paper bookmark
Copy the price from the shelf
Use the maker's name as your own
questions.answer: Draw crossing bands on a paper bookmark
hints: Borrow a visible feature for a different use.
questions.explanation: Borrow a visible feature for a different use. Draw crossing bands on a paper bookmark.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which idea could still be shared in a different version?

The class values working together
People use the shore as a landing place
Keeping drains clear lets water pass

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Which source could help a pupil develop the subject further?

A labelled account of Theodosia Okoh's flag design

questions.stem: You need three ideas for showing a tree. Which set gives three real alternatives?
options: A leaf rubbing, a cut-paper tree and a clay model
Three copies of the same unchanged outline
Three prices for one pencil
The same drawing signed three times
questions.answer: A leaf rubbing, a cut-paper tree and a clay model
hints: Change the way the subject is shown.
questions.explanation: Change the way the subject is shown. A leaf rubbing, a cut-paper tree and a clay model.

questions.stem: Two tiny sketches show different views of a stall. Why look at both?
options: To avoid choosing a viewpoint
To decide which sheet has the neatest back
To decide which view shows the action better
To count who sharpened a pencil first
questions.answer: To decide which view shows the action better
hints: A change in viewpoint can reveal a detail.
questions.explanation: A change in viewpoint can reveal a detail. To decide which view shows the action better.

questions.stem: Which research question could inspire a new work about a place?
options: Which seat will the teacher use?
How many letters are in our classroom number?
What is the price of the display tape?
What details would someone who lives here notice?
questions.answer: What details would someone who lives here notice?
hints: Ideas often begin with noticing something specific.
questions.explanation: Ideas often begin with noticing something specific. What details would someone who lives here notice?.

questions.stem: You have three ideas on separate cards. Two seem to tell parts of one story. What could you try?
options: Remove both because they are similar
Choose a fourth idea without reading the cards
Combine the two and check whether the story still makes sense
Place them together and skip checking the result
questions.answer: Combine the two and check whether the story still makes sense
hints: Check what the combination communicates.
questions.explanation: Check what the combination communicates. Combine the two and check whether the story still makes sense.

questions.stem: Which choice develops a symbol for sharing?
options: Draw the border first and leave the subject undecided
Write a different date at every corner
Copy a picture of an empty wall
Try two hands passing one bowl between them

questions.stem: Your first idea is hard to recognise. What would be a useful next step?
options: Make the title a secret
Ask a partner what clue they noticed and revise it
Change the subject without looking at the work
Add more details at random

questions.stem: A pupil wants to show that one figure is important. Which sketch is worth trying?

Make every part equally hard to see
Draw only the title and leave out all figures
Give that figure more space than the others

questions.stem: You cannot visit the place you want to study. What could still help you develop an idea?

Choose a random place and call it the same one
Use labelled pictures or recordings from that place
Copy a friend's guess as a first-hand account

questions.explanation: Use evidence that identifies the place. Use labelled pictures or recordings from that place.

questions.stem: After studying Theodosia Okoh's design for Ghana's flag, pupils design a class flag with joined hands at its centre. Use the example to invent two ideas for a visual artwork about a group represented by its flag. Show one idea and say how it differs from the example.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. What subject should the reviewers keep in mind?
options: Checking a rumour before passing it on
Passing memories between generations
Passengers arriving and waiting
Valuing a shared home
questions.answer: Passengers arriving and waiting
hints: Identify the action or subject at the centre.
questions.explanation: The described action centres on passengers arriving and waiting.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which detail could the class use when trying out its guide?
options: The interrupted pupil receiving the speaking token
A second voice asking for the source
Two groups exchanging short sung lines
Quick steps changing to a still line
questions.answer: Quick steps changing to a still line
hints: Look for a detail the example actually describes.
questions.explanation: The evidence in the example is quick steps changing to a still line.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which method should the guide help the class discuss?
options: Arranging a call and a sung reply
Contrasting moving and held shapes
Alternating solo verses with a shared refrain
Using contrasting characters in dialogue
questions.answer: Contrasting moving and held shapes
hints: Think about how the parts were made or performed.
questions.explanation: The example uses contrasting moving and held shapes to show passengers arriving and waiting.

questions.stem: Which question helps review a dance?
options: What is the length of the programme cover?
What is the price of the curtain?
How do the movements and changes of level express the idea?
How many chairs stayed outside?
questions.answer: How do the movements and changes of level express the idea?
hints: Look at what the dancers do.
questions.explanation: Look at what the dancers do. How do the movements and changes of level express the idea?.

questions.stem: Which point belongs in a guide for judging spoken lines?
options: Can the words be heard and understood?
How many people signed the invitation?
How costly is the stage floor?
How many colours are on the ticket?
questions.answer: Can the words be heard and understood?
hints: Listen for clear speech.
questions.explanation: Listen for clear speech. Can the words be heard and understood?.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. What meaning could a reviewer check against the details?
options: Different voices can express a shared attachment to home
A busy station has moments of motion and waiting
Carrying waste away helps protect the river
Check information before sharing it
questions.answer: A busy station has moments of motion and waiting
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: The detail of quick steps changing to a still line supports the idea that a busy station has moments of motion and waiting.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which source would help reviewers understand the setting?
options: A teacher-provided example of a corrected public notice
A station worker's account of the morning queue
A credited recording of a song by Ephraim Amu
A teacher-provided account of class discussion in the school studied
questions.answer: A station worker's account of the morning queue
hints: Choose evidence about the actual subject.
questions.explanation: The closest source for this subject is a station worker's account of the morning queue.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which sentence describes evidence before giving an opinion?
options: The work will win first prize.
Quick steps changing to a still line.
Everybody will like the finished piece.
The maker must have found the work easy.
questions.answer: Quick steps changing to a still line.
hints: Choose a detail you can check in the example.
questions.explanation: Quick steps changing to a still line. This detail can be checked without guessing what someone thinks.

questions.stem: Which question asks a viewer for evidence about teamwork?
options: Which group has the most friends in the audience?
Who has the newest costume?
Which audience member came earliest?
At which cue did the performers enter together?
questions.answer: At which cue did the performers enter together?
hints: Look or listen for a shared action.
questions.explanation: Look or listen for a shared action. At which cue did the performers enter together?.

questions.stem: Which guide point suits a play?
options: Is the tallest actor always in the middle?
Do the characters' actions help the audience follow the story?
Is the programme longer than the script?
Did the earliest rehearsal have the most visitors?
questions.answer: Do the characters' actions help the audience follow the story?
hints: Think about how drama makes a story clear.
questions.explanation: Think about how drama makes a story clear. Do the characters' actions help the audience follow the story?.

questions.stem: What is a good way to record two reviewers' different ideas?
options: Write each view with the detail that supports it
Keep only the view of the taller reviewer
Change one view so both sentences match
Report that neither person looked at the piece
questions.answer: Write each view with the detail that supports it
hints: Keep the reasons alongside the views.
questions.explanation: Keep the reasons alongside the views. Write each view with the detail that supports it.

questions.stem: Which question asks about the way a work was made?
options: What is the length of the school term?
How many visitors came by bus?
Who finished lunch first?
How did the maker use the materials or actions?
questions.answer: How did the maker use the materials or actions?
hints: Ask about artistic choices.
questions.explanation: Ask about artistic choices. How did the maker use the materials or actions?.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which change could the guide help the maker assess?
options: Hold the queue shape for two beats longer
Pause before the question so its words are clear
Repeat the opening line when the pupil finally gets a turn
Lower the call's final note to make room for the reply
questions.answer: Hold the queue shape for two beats longer
hints: Keep the aim and strengthen the clue the audience needs.
questions.explanation: This change helps the audience notice quick steps changing to a still line.

questions.stem: Which contrast would make waiting stand out in a dance about a lorry station?
options: A costume change while every movement stays the same
A line of passengers hidden behind the arriving group
Quick steps by every dancer for the whole piece
Quick arrivals followed by a held line of passengers
questions.answer: Quick arrivals followed by a held line of passengers
hints: Compare motion with stillness.
questions.explanation: Compare motion with stillness. Quick arrivals followed by a held line of passengers.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. A partner wants to know why the artist chose this method. Which reply explains the choice?
options: It guarantees that everyone will have the same feeling.
It proves this is the only way to make the piece.
It helps show passengers arriving and waiting.
It shows the artist used the most costly tools.
questions.answer: It helps show passengers arriving and waiting.
hints: Ask what this choice helps the audience notice.
questions.explanation: Contrasting moving and held shapes helps communicate the subject through quick steps changing to a still line.

questions.stem: A guide says good dance must always be fast. What change makes the guide fairer?
options: Apply the rule only to friends.
Give a prize to the fastest dancer in every piece.
Ask whether the chosen speed suits the dance's idea.
Replace fast with loud for all dances.
questions.answer: Ask whether the chosen speed suits the dance's idea.
hints: Different ideas can need different speeds.
questions.explanation: Different ideas can need different speeds. Ask whether the chosen speed suits the dance's idea.

questions.stem: What shows that a judging guide is useful?
options: It predicts which friend will win a prize
It lists more words than any other guide
Every reviewer gives the same mark without discussion
Reviewers can use it to explain what worked and suggest a change
questions.answer: Reviewers can use it to explain what worked and suggest a change
hints: A guide should lead to reasoned comments.
questions.explanation: A guide should lead to reasoned comments. Reviewers can use it to explain what worked and suggest a change.

questions.stem: A review sheet asks about a prop's purpose. Which note fits?
options: The empty bowl helped us understand that the character needed food.
The actor's name was written in blue.
The audience came in after lunch.
The hall has a metal roof.
questions.answer: The empty bowl helped us understand that the character needed food.

questions.explanation: Connect the stage object to the story. The empty bowl helped us understand that the character needed food.

questions.stem: Which question asks about purpose?

How many people stood near the door?
Who brought the newest shoes?

questions.answer: What is this piece trying to help its audience understand or do?

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Make two rules with a partner for discussing a performance about passengers arriving and waiting. Try one rule on the example and give a reason for your view.

questions.explanation: For example, connect quick steps changing to a still line to the idea that a busy station has moments of motion and waiting. Other supported choices are welcome.

Two groups exchanging short sung lines
A character carrying a waste bag back from the river
Quick steps changing to a still line
questions.answer: Quick steps changing to a still line
hints: Look for a detail the example actually describes.
questions.explanation: The evidence in the example is quick steps changing to a still line.

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which method can the reviewer identify from the description?
options: Using contrasting characters in dialogue
Contrasting moving and held shapes
Arranging a call and a sung reply
Using mime and a simple prop
questions.answer: Contrasting moving and held shapes
hints: Think about how the parts were made or performed.
questions.explanation: The example uses contrasting moving and held shapes to show passengers arriving and waiting.

questions.stem: A group sings well together but the words disappear under a shaker. What feedback fits?

Ask the audience to guess the missing words.
Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.
Change every singer's name in the programme.
questions.answer: Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.
hints: Identify a strength and a change to the balance.
questions.explanation: Identify a strength and a change to the balance. Keep the group singing and soften the shaker under the words.

questions.stem: What is useful feedback about a chorus the audience was invited to sing?
options: The curtain should cost more.
The returning words were clear, but we needed a cue for our entrance.
The hall has a large store cupboard.
The invitation was on white paper.
questions.answer: The returning words were clear, but we needed a cue for our entrance.
hints: Consider what helped or hindered participation.
questions.explanation: Consider what helped or hindered participation. The returning words were clear, but we needed a cue for our entrance.

questions.stem: A viewer says a dance showed excitement. Which detail supports that view?

questions.stem: The main part was missed by several people. Which suggestion could help?

Report that everyone noticed it
Change the maker's name

questions.stem: How can a group see whether its revision helped?

Assume the second version must be clearer

questions.stem: A dance based on a Ghanaian lorry station uses quick steps for arriving passengers and a still line for the queue. Which suggestion gives the maker a specific next step?

questions.stem: Which contrast would make waiting stand out in a dance about a lorry station?
